channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh-Korean Center for Rare Metals Technologies Opens
item.description: A new Kazakh-Korean Center for Rare Metals Technologies has been inaugurated. This center aims to foster collaboration and advancements in the field of rare metals between Kazakhstan and South Korea.

item.title: Tajikistan Seeks Japanese Expertise for Industrial Development
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies met with JICA's Vice President to discuss cooperation in vocational training and skill enhancement. Tajikistan aims to leverage Japan's experience for its industrial sector development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's First Lady Visits Children's Rehabilitation Center in Samarkand
item.description: Aygul Japarova, the First Lady of Kyrgyzstan, attended the opening of the IMKON specialized kindergarten and rehabilitation center in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The center offers early childhood education, medical rehabilitation, and psychological support for children. This visit occurred during a summit on child well-being and a congress on pediatric oncology.

item.title: Activist Sanzhar Bokaev Faces Five Charges as Trial Begins in Almaty
item.description: Civil activist Sanzhar Bokaev, along with his relative Madiyar Kalmenov and videographer Ulan Nusipkozha, is on trial in Almaty. Bokaev faces charges on five counts. A key witness was reportedly detained by police outside the courthouse as the proceedings commenced. Bokaev has been in custody since March 2026.

item.title: Aktau domestic violence case sparks public outrage
item.description: An investigation is underway in Aktau following a severe domestic violence incident where a man allegedly beat his partner, breaking four of her front teeth and shaving her head. The victim's mother stated the abuse was systematic. The perpetrators are identified as citizens of Uzbekistan, reportedly without proper documentation in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's tourism sector sees significant investment growth
item.description: Kazakhstan's tourism industry is experiencing substantial growth, with investments exceeding $4.8 billion. Funds are directed towards new hotels and mountain resort development. The government is also improving transport infrastructure in tourist areas to accommodate a rise in foreign visitors. Over 328 tourism projects are currently underway.

item.title: Self-Combustion of Waste Detected at Landfills in Kant and Ivanovka, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Self-combustion and smoldering of waste have been observed at landfills in Kant and Ivanovka, Chuy region, Kyrgyzstan. The Ministry of Natural Resources investigated, finding that landfill gas (methane) accumulation from decomposing organic matter causes temperatures to reach 60-80 degrees Celsius. This poses a risk of spontaneous combustion, especially in unregulated sites emitting toxic gases.

item.title: Kazakhstan Men's Table Tennis Team Advances in Asian Championship
item.description: The Kazakhstan men's table tennis team is progressing well at the Asian Championship in Tashkent, defeating the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia. They are set to face Iraq for a quarter-final spot. The women's team, despite a win against Mongolia, lost to Malaysia.

item.title: Criminal Cases Investigated in Almaty Over Pensioner Housing Fraud
item.description: Several criminal cases are under investigation in Almaty concerning the fraudulent seizure of housing from elderly residents. This year, individuals accused of kidnapping an 81-year-old pensioner and forcing him to sign over his apartment were sent to trial. Suspects in the murder of a 61-year-old man, possibly linked to property fraud, have been apprehended.

item.title: Almaty Residents Complain About Construction Dust Despite Warnings
item.description: Almaty residents continue to report hazardous dust from construction and road work, with complaints persisting for months. The city's Akim (mayor) has noted systematic violations in work organization, including dust, nighttime noise, and unsafe passages. Despite previous warnings to contractors, the issue remains unresolved, with new complaints emerging regularly.

item.title: Turkestan Region Faces Ecological Scandal as Sewage Pollutes District
item.description: An ecological scandal is unfolding in the Tolebi district of Turkestan region, where sewage from residential buildings, private homes, and a hospital flows openly, polluting the soil and forming a large lake. Residents complain of foul odors and poor drinking water quality due to damaged pipes and non-functional treatment facilities. Budgeted funds for repairs are questioned.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Electricity Production Up 8.4%, Imports Down 27.2% in First Nine Months
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Uzbekistan generated 69.6 billion kWh of electricity, an 8.4% increase. Green energy production reached last year's annual output during the same period. Electricity imports decreased by 27.2%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov to Visit Jalal-Abad Region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov will undertake a working visit to the Jalal-Abad region today. During the trip, he will meet with residents, hear reports from local authorities on the socio-economic situation, and review the region's development prospects. The visit aims to assess current conditions and future growth opportunities.

item.title: Tajikistan to Receive $20.5 Million for Pension System Digitalization
item.description: Tajikistan and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) signed a grant agreement in Dushanbe for the "Social Insurance System Modernization and Digitalization" project. The $20.5 million project, funded by ADB and the High-Tech Development Fund, aims to improve social insurance and pension services, expand coverage, and modernize delivery mechanisms.

item.title: Turkey, Pakistan, Qatar, Indonesia Sign Defense Industry Cooperation Pact
item.description: Four nations have signed a multilateral memorandum of understanding in Doha, Qatar, to cooperate in the defense industry. The 'Badr' agreement aims to develop joint production projects, military technologies, and train specialists.

item.title: Russia Ready to Resume Talks with Ukraine and US in November
item.description: Following a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, the Kremlin announced its readiness to resume trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the United States in November. Assistant to the Russian President Yuri Ushakov stated that the talks would focus on establishing a security system for both nations post-conflict. Abu Dhabi is a potential venue for the meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Transition to Two-Stage Conscription Model by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a military reform, including a transition to a two-stage conscription model by 2027. The reform aims to create a modern, mobile, and technologically advanced army, focusing on improved command, training, and equipment. The interaction between the army and society will also be re-evaluated.

item.title: Khartoum Airport Attacked by Drones Amidst Escalating Sudan Conflict
item.description: Khartoum International Airport and other areas of the capital have been targeted by drone attacks, reportedly linked to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), amid escalating conflict in Sudan. The attacks, which followed deadly strikes in Kordofan and Abyei, caused flight disruptions. Several civilians were reported killed in the capital.

item.title: Switzerland and China Support Tajikistan's Economy with New Regional Program
item.description: Switzerland will continue supporting Tajikistan through a new regional cooperation program for 2026-2029, with a total budget of 154.4 million Swiss francs for Central Asia. Funding will focus on water resources, energy, sustainable economic development, human rights, and civil society. China also supports Tajikistan's economy.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Transition to Two-Stage Military Service Model
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning a military reform that includes restructuring forces, improving command and control, establishing drone units, and strengthening army components. A key aspect is a shift to a two-stage conscript service: six months of training followed by six months of operational duty in military units. Measures to ensure soldier safety and rights are also planned.

item.title: European Government Websites Disabled Due to Vulnerability in Popular PHP Programming Language
item.description: Government websites across Europe and other nations have been taken offline following the discovery of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Developers have released urgent patches, warning that these flaws, present for years, affect a significant portion of the internet and necessitate immediate updates or site deactivation.

item.title: New Projects and Industrial Growth Transform Kashkadarya into a Leading Region
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Kashkadarya region, inspecting a new textile factory in the 'Kashkadarya' free economic zone. The $54 million project created 840 jobs and boasts advanced water and energy-saving technologies, including a closed-loop water system and solar panels, significantly reducing production costs and environmental impact.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prepares for Return of 13 Citizens from Ukraine War Zone
item.description: Thirteen Kazakh citizens, whose families advocated for their return from the conflict zone in Ukraine, are being prepared for repatriation. Lawyer Meirman Shekeev confirmed that no obstacles currently prevent their return and emphasized the need for a safe journey home. Families expressed gratitude to the President of Kazakhstan and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their assistance.

item.title: C5+1 Summit in Samarkand Yields Joint Statement on Partnership and Future Cooperation
item.description: The C5+1 summit in Samarkand, involving foreign ministers from the US and five Central Asian nations, concluded with a Joint Statement titled 'C5+1: Historic Partnership, Prosperous Future.' Key outcomes include enhanced trade, investment, transport cooperation via the Trans-Caspian route, collaboration on critical minerals, energy security, technology, counter-terrorism, and educational exchanges.

item.title: Turkey and Uzbekistan Adapt Cities to Changing Climate Conditions
item.description: Turkey and Uzbekistan are implementing strategies to make their cities more resilient to climate change impacts like heat, floods, and droughts. Turkey focuses on infrastructure and renewable energy, while Uzbekistan is developing New Tashkent and adapting its existing capital.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Judicial Oversight: What Judges Must Verify Before Detaining Suspects
item.description: Starting July 1, 2027, Uzbekistani judges must verify sufficient grounds for suspicion or accusation before approving detention. This reform expands judicial oversight, requiring judges to examine evidence and ensure procedural compliance, moving beyond mere legality checks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores Economic Diplomacy with Oman, Japan, Italy, and Germany
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is analyzing efforts to strengthen economic diplomacy. The Ambassador to Oman met with the head of the Real Estate Association to discuss cooperation. In Japan, agreements were reached to expand trade and investment. Uzbekistan showcased its tourism potential at an exhibition in Italy and discussed agricultural modernization with Germany.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Domestic violence case investigated in Aktau after woman reports assault
item.description: Police in Aktau, Kazakhstan, have opened a criminal case following a woman's report of severe assault by her husband. The victim claims he knocked out her teeth and cut her hair after an argument about rent. Both individuals are reportedly citizens of Uzbekistan without valid identification documents for staying in Kazakhstan. The man has been detained.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Kindergarten teacher accused of child abuse in Zhambyl region
item.description: Parents in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region have accused a kindergarten teacher of abusing their two-year-old son, reporting visible bruises. The kindergarten initially claimed the child was injured in a fight with other children, later stating the teacher accidentally hit him while separating them. Parents demand an investigation into alleged concealment of facts.

item.title: Zelensky Willing to Freeze Ukraine Conflict Along Current Front Lines
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated his readiness to halt hostilities with Russia along the current front lines, expressing this in an interview with Fox News. He affirmed willingness to accept a peace deal that freezes the conflict, provided Ukraine retains control over at least 75% of its territory. Zelensky rejected proposals to cede Donbas for peace, emphasizing the need for diplomatic solutions based on current positions.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts Discussion on Modern Water Resource Management Technologies
item.description: Tashkent hosted an event focusing on energy efficiency, rational water resource use, and industrial technology modernization. A key aspect was the partnership between "EBA Engineering," "ARC Water & Energy," and Danish pump manufacturer "Grundfos." EBA Engineering became Grundfos's industrial sector distributor in Uzbekistan, aiming to optimize, decarbonize, and transform water management through advanced equipment and technical support.

item.title: Kazakhstan and EU Trade Turnover Reaches $31.6 Billion
item.description: The 9th meeting of the Cooperation Committee on Trade between Kazakhstan and the European Union was held in Brussels. The parties discussed the current state and development prospects of trade-economic and investment cooperation. Issues of removing barriers and restrictions in mutual trade were also addressed. The implementation of the Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement was a key focus.

item.title: EU Allocates €12 Million for Essential Services in Afghanistan
item.description: The European Union has allocated €12 million to provide healthcare, nutrition, and water services to over 347,000 people in southern and southwestern Afghanistan. The assistance, delivered through INTERSOS in cooperation with other organizations, will run from June 2026 to May 2027. It aims to support vulnerable populations and prevent diseases and deaths.

item.title: EU Allocates €12 Million for Aid to Vulnerable People in Afghanistan
item.description: The European Union has allocated €12 million for vital services in health, nutrition, protection, and water and sanitation for crisis-affected people in six southern and southwestern provinces of Afghanistan. The funding will support a 12-month project benefiting 347,000 individuals, with indirect benefits for nearly 1.27 million others.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Compulsory Military Service to Be Divided into Two Stages
item.description: Kazakhstan's Armed Forces are transitioning to a two-stage model for compulsory military service. The first six months will involve basic military training in specialized centers, followed by six months of practical combat training and task execution in military units. Reforms also focus on soldier safety and rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Latin Alphabet Law to Take Effect in April 2027
item.description: A new Uzbek alphabet based on Latin script, signed by the President on October 21, will come into force on April 22, 2027. Documents issued before this date will remain valid. The government has two months to develop an implementation plan for the new alphabet, which features 28 letters and an apostrophe.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Large-Scale Army Reform
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved a significant reform of its armed forces. The details of the reform were not immediately disclosed, but it is expected to modernize the military and enhance its capabilities. This move signals a commitment to strengthening national defense and security within the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Passport Ranking Declines in Henley & Partners Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has dropped to 81st place in the Henley & Partners Passport Index for October 2026, sharing the position with Sao Tome and Principe. Holders can access 59 destinations visa-free. This marks a decline from the 75th position earlier in the year. Kazakhstan's passport remains the strongest in Central Asia at 66th place.

item.title: President's Book on Turkmen Neutrality Published in Azerbaijani
item.description: A presentation ceremony was held for the Azerbaijani translation of President Serdar Berdimuhamedow's book 'Turkmenistan's Neutrality - A Clear Path to Peace and Trust'. The publication highlights Turkmenistan's foreign policy focused on global peace and good neighborliness, as recognized by the UN. The book details the goals and achievements of Turkmenistan's neutrality policy.

item.title: International Oil and Gas Forum Held in Ashgabat
item.description: The "Turkmenistan Oil and Gas - 2026" international conference and exhibition has commenced in Ashgabat. Turkmenistan, a leading energy state with vast natural gas reserves, aims to expand energy partnerships and integrate innovative technologies. Organized by state concerns, the event facilitates direct relations, new projects, and global experience exchange.
